implementation_notes: kotlinx.coroutines ships the channel: MutableSharedFlow is a hot flow that shares emitted values among all its collectors in a broadcast fashion, so every collector receives every emission; MutableSharedFlow(extraBufferCapacity = N, onBufferOverflow = DROP_OLDEST) is the idiomatic application event bus, replacing a hand-written listener registry. Collectors must run in coroutines (collect/launchIn), which makes delivery cancelable; keep a plain listener list when the publisher cannot suspend. Without buffer capacity, emit() rendezvous with all subscribers and tryEmit() succeeds only when nobody is subscribed.
pitfalls: Without extraBufferCapacity or replay, emit() suspends until every subscriber has received the value and tryEmit() on such a flow succeeds only when there are no subscribers - the emitted value is then silently lost.
A shared flow never completes and emission cost is O(N) in subscribers; collectors that stop collecting (cancelled scope) silently stop receiving while the flow keeps broadcasting.
flowOn and buffer() with RENDEZVOUS capacity are no-ops on a shared flow, so back-pressure must be configured at construction.
